findings.source: Agent.sol:105-144 for (i < protectedTokensLength) { require(_target != token); protectedTokens_[i] = token; balances[i] = balance(token); } bool result = _target.call(_data); ... for (j < protectedTokensLength) {...} emit SafeExecute(...); return
findings.issue: Because the code after each loop ends in return or revert, the decompiler prints it inside the loop as the exit branch of 'while True: if i >= n:', so the first loop's actual body appears some 200 lines after its header, after the second loop; the semantics are right but the program order is inverted.
findings.rule: When a loop's exit block never comes back to the loop, print 'while not exit_cond: body' followed by the exit block (the exit block dominates nothing in the body), instead of nesting the exit block in the loop head.

findings.source: new address[](protectedTokensLength); new uint256[](...); balance(token) -> token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(ERC20.balanceOf.selector, this))
findings.issue: Zeroing a new memory array by copying code from beyond the end of the bytecode (offset 16282 = code size) reads as a copy, and the balanceOf selector stored as a 4-byte slice prints in decimal.
findings.rule: CODECOPY from an offset >= code size yields zeros: print 'mem[a len n] = 0'; print a constant stored as a 4-byte slice in hex.
